items.stem: Explain the Tyndall effect. Why is it visually observed in a mixture of milk and water but never in a simple mixture of common salt and water?
items.answer: The Tyndall effect is the optical scattering of a beam of light by suspended microscopic particles in a mixture, essentially making the straight path of the light beam clearly visible. Milk mixed with water forms a heterogeneous colloidal emulsion, which contains large dispersed fat particles (between 1 nm and 1000 nm) that successfully scatter incoming light. Conversely, salt dissolved in water forms a true homogeneous solution. The completely dissolved salt particles are incredibly tiny, measuring less than 1 nm, which is far too small to scatter light.

items.stem: Define the related processes of sublimation and deposition. Provide one clear example of a solid heterogeneous mixture that can be quickly separated by directly exploiting this unique property.
items.answer: Sublimation is the highly fascinating physical process where a solid completely changes directly into a hot gaseous state upon active heating, entirely bypassing the usual intermediate liquid phase. Conversely, deposition is the exact reverse transition where a cooling gas rapidly transforms directly back into a cold solid without ever becoming liquid. A perfect daily example of a mixture safely separated using this thermal property is crushed camphor heavily mixed with normal sand. When gently heated, only the camphor rapidly sublimes, effectively leaving the non-sublimable sand completely behind.

items.stem: Explain in detailed scientific terms why the process of crystallization is widely considered a significantly better technique for purifying solid chemical substances compared to the simple boiling evaporation method.
items.answer: Crystallization is vastly superior to the simple evaporation technique because it consistently yields a substantially purer final solid product. During aggressive evaporation, a liquid solution is heated completely to absolute dryness, effectively ensuring that any previously dissolved soluble impurities remain permanently mixed within the final resulting solid residue. Furthermore, delicate organic compounds like edible sugar can easily char or decompose upon continuous intense heating. During crystallization, perfectly pure solid separates out neatly into geometric patterns from a gradually cooling saturated solution, leaving all unwanted chemical impurities harmlessly suspended in the liquid.

items.stem: Compare biological colloids and standard suspensions explicitly with respect to their average microscopic particle size and their natural ability to physically settle down when left completely undisturbed over time.
items.answer: Colloids contain moderately sized active particles usually ranging anywhere between 1 nanometer and 1000 nanometers in their physical diameter. When left entirely undisturbed on a flat surface, biological colloidal particles stubbornly remain uniformly dispersed throughout their liquid medium and absolutely never settle down, ensuring incredible stability. items.stem: Describe exactly how the technique of paper chromatography is efficiently utilized in a chemistry laboratory to safely separate the distinctly different coloured chemical dyes currently present in a single black ink spot.
items.answer: Paper chromatography efficiently separates mixed chemical components strictly based upon their distinctly different natural rates of physical movement along a highly porous paper surface. A tiny spot of black ink is gently placed near the absolute bottom edge of a filter paper strip. This paper is subsequently dipped partially into a liquid solvent like water. As the liquid slowly rises upward through the paper fibres via natural capillary action, it actively carries the dissolved dye molecules. The highly soluble dyes travel much faster, successfully separating the distinct colours vertically.

items.stem: Draw a simple mechanical diagram properly illustrating the industrial process of active centrifugation. Explain clearly how this unique rapid technique successfully separates heavy solid microscopic particles from a large liquid mixture.
items.answer: Industrial centrifugation involves forcefully spinning a fluid mixture rapidly inside a closed tube at incredibly high speeds. When this sealed tube constantly rotates in a violent circular motion, a massive outward centrifugal force strongly acts upon the fluid contents. This intense physical force rapidly pushes the much denser, substantially heavier solid particles outward, mechanically forcing them to rapidly clump and settle down at the extreme bottom of the spinning tube. The much lighter liquid portion safely remains at the absolute top, ensuring a perfectly clean fluid separation.

items.answer: (a) To obtain pure copper sulfate, dissolve the impure sample in a minimum amount of water with a drop of dilute sulfuric acid. Heat the mixture gently to prepare a saturated solution. Filter this hot liquid to remove insoluble impurities. Finally, allow the clear filtrate to cool slowly without disturbance. Secondly, evaporation leaves all soluble impurities mixed directly with the newly dried solid. Crystallization successfully isolates the pure compound because the soluble impurities remain fully dissolved within the leftover solvent instead of incorporating into the newly formed solid crystal lattice.
